title: Control the nonlinear comparison with a polynomial reference-amplitude bound
statement: On a preserved fibre let X multiply by m=k_j. For initial low cutoffN, ||B_ij|| and||[X,B_ij]||<=2piN, so during a nonnegative pulse of total impulse theta and subsequent heat, ||Xa||2<=N(1+2pi theta)M. One-dimensional Fourier Cauchy-Schwarz and finitely many preserved fibres give ||a||infinity²<=2^16 M²(N+1)^3(1+theta), polynomial rather than exponential in impulse. Choose theta=q^10,K=q^6,delta=q^-40,T=ell/(nu q^12): nonlinear relative-energy coefficient is O(q^10), stage duration O(q^-12), hence their product O(q^-2) tends tozero. Pure-transport Laplacian bound<=2^15 N²(1+theta)² M makes pulse viscosity error O(q^-20). These explicit controls remove the mixing-strength/nonlinear-error circularity for the exact no-stretching equation; they do not imply strong uniqueness or practical pulse sizes.
